rules.title: Advice to the reader, not a fact
rules.text: A document states what is true. 'You should', 'just run', 'feel free to' address a reader who is about to find the same thing in the step that follows, or in the contract above.

inspection.pattern: (?i)\b(you (should|need to|have to|must|will want to)|if you (want|need|prefer|like)|just (run|use|add|set|call|try)|simply (run|use|add|set)|feel free to|you'?ll want)\b

judgement.question: Is this advice addressed to the reader — what they should do or will want — rather than a statement about the subject (what the caller piped, what the script does, what the contract requires)?

criteria.true: it instructs or reassures the reader, and the step next to it, or the contract above it, already says the same thing
criteria.false: the second person is the contract's own subject ('the evidence you piped', 'options you defined') or part of a command's quoted output
